---
title: "Week 7 · Multiple linear regression. Practice"
subtitle: "Three worked examples end to end: hedonic land prices, a rice production function, and returns to fertiliser in a field experiment"
---

The final week applies everything: each example goes from problem setting and
model formulation through exploratory analysis, estimation, interpretation,
checking linearity and re-specifying the model, to a conclusion. The third
example shows how regression is used to read the results of a randomised
experiment.

## What the deck covers

-   **Causal interpretation of the MLR**: multiple regression controls only for
    the factors included in the model; external ceteris paribus is assumed;
    the regression assumptions restated.
-   **Example 1, a hedonic land prices model**: problem setting, regression
    model formulation, exploratory analysis (summary statistics, regional
    differences, distributions, scatter plots), estimating the regression,
    interpreting the results, checking linearity, re-specifying the model and
    re-checking, and comparing the two models.
-   **Example 2, a production function**: problem setting, the regression model
    and ex-ante hypotheses about the coefficients, exploratory analysis
    including the effect of the BIMAS programme, estimating the regression and
    interpreting it coefficient by coefficient, checking linearity, moving to
    a log specification, interpreting the log model, and conclusions.
-   **Example 3, returns to fertiliser in Kenya**: objective and results of the
    field experiment, whether ceteris paribus is ensured in the RCT, the
    authors' regression solution, and checks and balances.
-   **Regression in Excel**: a pointer for those who do not use R.

## Data used

-   `MinnLand` (Minnesota farmland sales) from the alr4 R package, for the
    hedonic land prices model.
-   `RiceFarms` (Indonesian rice farms) from the plm R package, for the
    production function.
-   Tables of the published field experiment, as images in
    [`materials/img`](https://github.com/EBukin/mk68-2023-24-public/tree/main/materials/img).
